slots.title: US session recap — Nov. 6, 2026
slots.body:
The Nasdaq Composite led major U.S. benchmarks lower, closing at 24,315.00 (-5.5%, -1,421.52 points).
Coverage framed the session as an AI- and technology-led selloff that left the Nasdaq in correction territory after the election.

The S&P 500 finished at 7,353.73 (-4.4%, -334.89 points), with an intraday range between 7,350.35 and 7,681.29.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed at 51,523.06 (-3.4%, -1,833.06 points).

The Russell 2000 ended at 2,729.89 (-4.4%).

The VIX rose to 28.18 (+69.7%, +11.57), from a prior close of 16.61 — the largest one-day percentage jump in the injected tape for that gauge.

Semiconductor and AI-linked megacaps carried much of the equity story:
- $AMD -17.3% to 404.40
- $TSM -10.8% to 353.10
- $TSLA -10.8% to 343.69
- $AVGO -10.4% to 291.53
- $ASML -9.3% to 1,356.65
- $ORCL -7.0% to 115.06

with $ORCL’s session low at 111.66 matching its 52-week low in the data.
$NVDA, among the most active symbols in the feed, closed at 181.60 (-9.3%).

$INTC closed at 52.25 (-10.3%).
Leveraged semiconductor products reflected the same direction: $SOXL -38.7% to 40.87 while the bear 3x semiconductors ETF $SOXS +39.2% to 81.22.

Among megacaps outside chips,:
- $AAPL -1.5% to 344.17
- $AMZN -2.2% to 260.21
- $META -4.0% to 605.08

$BABA bucked the decline, +2.6% to 108.07.

$APP stood out among liquid advancers, +31.0% to 356.10.
$CHTR, on the earnings calendar for the date, closed +4.7% to 125.86; $MRNA, also scheduled to report, finished -6.5% to 241.46.

Overseas indexes in the feed showed risk-off tone after the U.S. tech move: Japan’s Nikkei 225 at 57,456.17 (-5.9%), with WSJ tying the drop to chip stocks after the U.S. technology selloff.
Hang Seng -1.2% to 24,494.00; FTSE 100 -0.4% to 10,782.66.

Oil-linked quotes firmed: Brent crude at 99.64 (+1.4%) and the USO ETF at 148.21 (+1.9%), while gold futures (GCUSD) settled at 4,055.20 (-1.4%).
Bitcoin (BTCUSD) was 75,477.26 (-0.7%).
The UUP dollar-bull ETF edged to 28.92 (+0.1%).

Treasury snapshot dated 2026-11-04 in the data showed the 10-year at 4.9% and a 2s10s spread of 0.32.

The economic calendar in the feed listed high-impact U.S. releases for Nov. 6 including October nonfarm payrolls (estimate 65K, prior 29K), unemployment rate (estimate 4.2%), and Michigan consumer sentiment for November (estimate 48); actual print values were not included in the injected close bundle.
